policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Behold' renders the imperative but does not distinguish the qere form הַבִּיטָה from ketiv הביט; no mapped textual note is supplied, so the base fallback is retained.
ASV 'orphans and fatherless' explicitly supplies the conjunction represented by qere וְאֵין, distinguishing it from ketiv אין.
ASV 'and have no rest' explicitly renders the conjunction represented by qere וְלֹא, distinguishing it from ketiv לא.
ASV 'and are not' explicitly renders the conjunction represented by qere וְאֵינָם, distinguishing it from ketiv אינם.
ASV 'And we have borne' explicitly renders the conjunction represented by qere וַאֲנַחְנוּ, distinguishing it from ketiv אנחנו.

ASV 'and we shall be turned' does not distinguish qere וְנָשׁוּבָה from ketiv ונשוב; both retain the conjunction and the English does not decide the final-he form, while no mapped textual note is supplied, so the base fallback is retained.
